review.overview: PR #403 stages a shared Railway Redis service, adds a typed @package/queue boundary with BullMQ and in-memory adapters, and moves the scraper producers and processor onto it while keeping the legacy scraper-queue. The assumed load is the existing single scheduled scraper service with BullMQ workers and a few producers, not many concurrent writers. The main risks are that the new queue has no volume in the visible plan, the Redis client stops reconnecting after three attempts, and shutdown can drop pending enqueues. The docs also tell operators to cut over immediately, which conflicts with the PR claim that cutover is separately approved.

findings.title: Staged queue writes to a volume the plan does not provision
findings.evidence: The sharedQueue start command writes RDB and AOF to $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH, but railway-config.test.mjs expects exactly four resources including only volume.redis-volume, which the legacy queue uses. No distinct volume is attached to sharedQueue in the visible plan.
findings.impact: If the env var is unset the redis-server start command receives --dir with no value and crash-loops. If Railway supplies ephemeral storage instead, AOF and RDB vanish on redeploy and the durable queue claim is false.
findings.recommendation: Attach a new volume to sharedQueue, for example pocket-trash-queue-volume, assert it in railway-config.test.mjs, and never mount redis-volume into two Redis services.

findings.title: Redis client gives up reconnecting after about two seconds
findings.evidence: retryStrategy returns null once times exceeds 3, so ioredis stops reconnecting after roughly 1.75 seconds. BullMQ workers are long-lived and expect the connection to recover.
findings.impact: A Redis restart, failover, or slow Railway deploy leaves the scraper process alive but unable to enqueue or process jobs until someone restarts it. Cron runs then fail silently.
findings.recommendation: Return a capped delay for every attempt on worker connections, and reserve fail-fast retry limits for short-lived commands or tests.

findings.title: Shutdown disconnects before pending commands flush
findings.evidence: close() calls connection.disconnect(), which closes the socket immediately instead of waiting for pending commands to flush.
findings.impact: On SIGTERM during an enqueue or completion ack, the command can be lost. Producers may drop jobs and workers may leave work unacknowledged.
findings.recommendation: Await connection.quit() after closing queues, with a short timeout that falls back to disconnect().

findings.title: Shared queue exposes a public Redis TCP proxy
findings.evidence: sharedQueue copies the legacy tcpProxies: { "6379": {} }, so the new Redis is reachable through a public TCP proxy. The docs say clients should use the private REDIS_URL and never copy the public endpoint.
findings.impact: The shared queue adds another internet-facing Redis endpoint protected only by a password, which increases brute-force and scanning exposure for no stated benefit.
findings.recommendation: Remove the TCP proxy from sharedQueue and keep only the private network endpoint, unless a documented external consumer needs public access.

findings.title: Docs prescribe a cutover the PR says is not approved
findings.evidence: The new paragraph tells operators to point the scraper and Discord bot at ${{pocket-trash-queue.REDIS_URL}}. The PR body says the legacy queue is retained and previews stay on it until a separately approved cutover, and deploy.yml changes no REDIS_URL.
findings.impact: An operator following the docs can switch the scraper to an empty queue before the approved cutover, leaving jobs already in scraper-queue unprocessed with no drain step.
findings.recommendation: State that existing services keep the legacy scraper-queue reference until the cutover PR, and move the switch instruction into that PR.

findings.title: Durability claim has no restart test
findings.evidence: The integration fixture starts Redis with --appendonly no and kills it without a restart. No test exercises the RDB and AOF flags or a Redis restart; railway-config.test.mjs only regex-matches the start command.
findings.impact: A missing volume or wrong persistence flag ships without a failing test, so the core durability claim of this PR is unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add one test that starts Redis with the production persistence flags, writes a key or job, restarts the process, and asserts the data survives. Assert the volume attachment in the Railway test as well.

review.overview: PR #354 adds a normalized Pens catalog schema covering market geography, source provenance and evidence, pens and parts, mechanisms, refill offerings, compatibility, terminology, and product configuration. The review covered the visible Drizzle schema, migration prefix, relations, catalog service, and tests. The main risks are an alias-concept migration that needs a backfill, a schema import cycle, containment cycles, and locking index builds on existing catalog tables.

findings.title: Alias concept_id migration needs a backfill for existing rows
findings.evidence: createAlias now fails when no catalog_terminology_concept matches (`if (!concept) throw new Error(...)`) and inserts only `conceptId`; existing catalog_terminology_alias rows were written with canonical_key and have no concept_id, and the visible migration prefix shows no concept seed or concept_id backfill.
findings.impact: Deploying with existing aliases either fails when concept_id is added NOT NULL or leaves old aliases unreadable through the new concept relation.
findings.recommendation: Seed concepts from existing namespace and key pairs, map every alias to its concept id, then set concept_id NOT NULL in the same migration; add an integration test that starts with a pre-existing alias.

findings.title: Schema modules form an import cycle
findings.evidence: collection.ts imports catalogTerminologyConcept from ./pens.js, while pens.ts imports collectionItem, finishOption, product, productImage, and productMaterial from ./collection.js.
findings.impact: ESM evaluates one side first; any non-lazy use of a table binding can throw 'Cannot access ... before initialization' or produce an undefined table at startup.
findings.recommendation: Move catalogTerminologyConcept into a neutral module imported by both schemas, or define the cross-schema reference only in relations.ts.

findings.title: Market containment accepts cycles
findings.evidence: catalog_market_containment only checks parent_market_id <> child_market_id; nothing prevents A containing B and B containing A, or longer cycles.
findings.impact: Recursive market rollups and ancestor or descendant queries can loop or return a wrong market scope.
findings.recommendation: Reject cycles with a deferred constraint trigger, or store the hierarchy in a closure table and validate inserts in one transaction.

findings.title: Unique constraints on existing catalog tables lock writes
findings.evidence: The PR adds unique("product_id_maker_unique") to product and unique("product_material_id_product_unique") to product_material at line 562, both existing tables.
findings.impact: The migration builds new unique indexes under an exclusive lock; on a large product catalog, writes block for the index build and the deploy can stall.
findings.recommendation: Check table sizes first. If they are large, create the indexes concurrently in a separate migration and attach the constraints afterward.

findings.title: Catalog tests no longer fail on extra product types
findings.evidence: Two exact resolves.toEqual([...]) assertions became resolves.toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([...])), so unexpected rows are ignored.
findings.impact: Duplicate or leaked product types can appear without failing the test, hiding seed and isolation bugs.
findings.recommendation: Filter by the test's maker or type IDs and assert the exact rows, or assert the expected length plus contents.

findings.title: updated_at is never refreshed on update
findings.evidence: entityTimestamps gives updatedAt only defaultNow(); the visible schema and migration define no BEFORE UPDATE trigger.
findings.impact: updated_at stays at insert time unless every service explicitly sets it, so ordering, cache invalidation, and audit views go stale.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared BEFORE UPDATE trigger, or set updated_at in every Pens update path and test it.

findings.title: Serial numbers are validated with trim but stored untrimmed
findings.evidence: collection_item_serial_number_valid uses char_length(trim(serial_number)) between 1 and 200, but serial_number itself is stored as plain text.
findings.impact: '123' and ' 123 ' are accepted as different values, so duplicate serials can coexist and lookups by exact value miss rows.
findings.recommendation: Add a check that serial_number = trim(serial_number), or normalize the value before insert.

review.overview: PR #354 adds the Pens catalog schema: a 1,407-line Drizzle module, a 1,145-line native migration, 587 lines of relations, catalog-service changes, integration tests, and a large schema-diagram update. The visible excerpts show a sound shared-primary-key and provenance design, but market code uniqueness, containment cycles, and alias namespace handling need correction before merge.

findings.title: Market code uniqueness blocks regions that share a country code
findings.evidence: `catalog_market` defines `"code" text NOT NULL CONSTRAINT "catalog_market_code_unique" UNIQUE`; `catalog_market_code_valid` then allows `kind = 'region'` codes of 2-40 characters, so a region code like `CA` cannot coexist with the country code `CA`.
findings.impact: A state or province market such as California or Ontario cannot be stored beside Canada, or must use a non-standard code that breaks code-based lookup.
findings.recommendation: Replace the column UNIQUE with `UNIQUE (kind, code)`, or require region codes to carry a country prefix such as `US-CA` and enforce that format in the CHECK.

findings.title: Region market codes are case-sensitive and not normalized
findings.evidence: The `region` branch of `catalog_market_code_valid` only checks `char_length(trim("code")) between 2 and 40 and "code" <> 'GLOBAL'`; it does not require uppercase, and the unique constraint is case-sensitive, so `us` and `US` both pass and both can be inserted.
findings.impact: Market lookup by code can miss rows depending on casing, and duplicate-looking markets pollute the hierarchy.
findings.recommendation: Add `code = upper(code)` for country and region, or use CITEXT, and compare `upper(code) <> 'GLOBAL'`.

findings.title: Market containment allows cycles and multiple parents
findings.evidence: `catalog_market_containment` has only `PRIMARY KEY (parent_market_id, child_market_id)` and `CHECK (parent_market_id <> child_market_id)`. Rows `(A,B)` and `(B,A)` both satisfy both constraints.
findings.impact: Recursive parent or ancestor queries can loop forever or return duplicate markets; a market can also have multiple parents, which may conflict with a tree model.
findings.recommendation: If containment is a tree, add `UNIQUE (child_market_id)`; otherwise add a recursive cycle check or trigger and document the DAG model.

findings.title: Containment child lookups have no supporting index
findings.evidence: The containment primary key is `(parent_market_id, child_market_id)`; no index begins with `child_market_id`. Finding a market's parents scans the whole table.
findings.impact: Ancestor resolution becomes O(n) per market as the hierarchy grows.
findings.recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX catalog_market_containment_child_idx ON catalog_market_containment (child_market_id);`.

findings.title: Alias creation hardcodes product-type namespace and input key
findings.evidence: The service looks up the concept with `input.canonicalNamespace` and `canonicalKey`, but the returned row overwrites `canonicalNamespace: "product-type"`; the insert also stores the input key rather than `concept.key`.
findings.impact: Aliases for any other namespace are reported as product-type, and a concept key that differs from the normalized input key splits the alias from its concept.
findings.recommendation: Return the namespace from the concept or input and use `concept.key` for `canonicalKey`; consider dropping the duplicated canonical columns now that `concept_id` exists.

findings.title: Product-type tests weakened to arrayContaining
findings.evidence: `listProductTypes` assertions changed from `resolves.toEqual([...])` to `resolves.toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([...]))` in two places.
findings.impact: Extra or duplicate product types now pass the test; the assertion no longer proves the service returns only the expected set.
findings.recommendation: Keep exact matching against a filtered result, or assert the length plus contents; seed the Pens product types explicitly in the test.

review.overview: PR #354 adds a normalized Pens catalog schema: shared-primary-key pen and part detail tables, mechanisms, refills, compatibility, markets and containment, source listings and evidence, and terminology concepts. It also adds a 1,145-line migration, central relation wiring, service lookup changes, integration tests, and an updated schema diagram. The visible hunks are broadly guarded by checks, but the review found a schema import cycle, non-updating updated_at columns, and a market hierarchy that permits cycles.

findings.title: Circular import between collection and pens schema modules
findings.evidence: collection.ts adds `import { catalogTerminologyConcept } from "./pens.js";`; pens.ts:18-24 imports `collectionItem`, `finishOption`, `product`, `productImage`, and `productMaterial` from `./collection.js`.
findings.impact: ESM finishes one module before the other, so a top-level use of the imported table can throw a temporal-dead-zone error; at minimum, drizzle-kit must resolve a cycle every time it loads the schema.
findings.recommendation: Move the concept table to a neutral module such as catalog-terminology.ts and import it from both schema files, keeping the import graph acyclic.

findings.title: updated_at never changes on row updates
findings.evidence: `entityTimestamps` at pens.ts:28-35 defines `updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true }).defaultNow().notNull()`; there is no `$onUpdate`, and the migration only sets `DEFAULT now()`.
findings.impact: Updates leave updated_at at the creation time, so cache invalidation, audit, and recent-change queries read stale values.
findings.recommendation: Add `.$onUpdate(() => new Date())` to the column or a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger that assigns `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`.

findings.title: Market containment allows cycles
findings.evidence: `catalog_market_containment` has PRIMARY KEY (parent_market_id, child_market_id) and only `CHECK ("parent_market_id" <> "child_market_id")`; nothing rejects A -> B plus B -> A.
findings.impact: Recursive market nesting or permission inheritance can loop indefinitely, and the hierarchy can store contradictory containment.
findings.recommendation: Reject cycles in an insert/update trigger with a recursive check, or document the acyclic contract and bound traversal depth in every consumer.

findings.title: No reverse index for market containment child
findings.evidence: The containment primary key is `(parent_market_id, child_market_id)`; `child_market_id` has no separate index in the visible migration.
findings.impact: Deleting or re-keying a market forces a sequential scan of containment for the FK check, and child-to-parent lookups are slow.
findings.recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX catalog_market_containment_child_idx ON catalog_market_containment (child_market_id);`.

findings.title: Composite unique indexes duplicate the primary key
findings.evidence: collection.ts:368 adds `unique("product_id_maker_unique").on(table.id, table.makerId)` and collection.ts:562 adds `unique("product_material_id_product_unique").on(table.id, table.productId)`; both `id` columns are already primary keys.
findings.impact: Each extra unique constraint writes and stores a second B-tree for a uniqueness rule the primary key already enforces; it only pays off if a composite FK targets it.
findings.recommendation: Confirm a composite FK needs these targets; otherwise drop both constraints and keep only the existing primary keys.

findings.title: Region market codes are validated untrimmed
findings.evidence: `catalog_market_code_valid` checks `char_length(trim("code"))` and `"code" <> 'GLOBAL'`, but `code` is stored and uniquely indexed as entered.
findings.impact: `'US '` and `'US'` both pass the region branch and coexist under the unique constraint, so code lookups and joins miss rows.
findings.recommendation: Add `CHECK ("code" = btrim("code"))` or normalize the value before insert, and make the case rule explicit.

findings.title: Redis adapter stops reconnecting after three attempts
findings.evidence: retryStrategy(times) returns `times <= 3 ? Math.min(times * 250, 1_000) : null`. After roughly 1.5s of failed reconnects ioredis is told to stop, and this adapter owns that connection for the whole process.
findings.impact: A Redis restart or network blip longer than about 1.5s permanently ends the queue connection. The cron scraper may recover on its next run, but the shared adapter is documented for the always-on Discord bot, where a worker would silently stop consuming until manually restarted.
findings.recommendation: Keep reconnecting for long-lived consumers with a capped backoff (never return null), or make the give-up policy an explicit adapter option that defaults to infinite for workers.

findings.title: Redis connection errors are swallowed with no signal
findings.evidence: `connection.on("error", () => { /* The operation waiting on Redis surfaces connection failures. */ });` installs an empty error handler.
findings.impact: Background connection failures (for example mid-outage or after retries are exhausted) produce no log, lifecycle event, or metric, so operators only notice a stalled queue from missing work.
findings.recommendation: Forward connection errors through the existing onEvent lifecycle callback and log them at warn/error level.

findings.title: Queue payload schemas duplicate TypeScript types and can drift

findings.title: Deferred validation triggers rescan whole tables on every row
findings.evidence: validate_product_configuration's required-slot check scans all of product_configuration_slot and rechecks every choice with no filter on the changed product (migration.sql:863-870); validate_refill_supporting_evidence (1012-1046) and validate_refill_market_conflicts (1066-1133) likewise scan their whole tables and the full market closure. Each is declared CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ... DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW (e.g. 873-875, 1049-1058).
findings.impact: Importing N configuration or refill rows fires N deferred trigger executions at commit, each scanning the whole table, so cost grows roughly quadratically; a large import or edit batch can stall the transaction.
findings.recommendation: Filter each validator to the affected product_id / offering_id derived from NEW/OLD and index the joined columns, so work is proportional to one entity instead of the table.

findings.title: Pen nose-profile carrier rule is not rechecked when a product is retyped
findings.evidence: validate_pen_nose_profile_carrier is attached only as AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON pen_nose_profile_assignment (migration.sql:812). The sibling product rule is attached as AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF product_type_id ON product (764), but the nose-profile rule has no product-table trigger.

LIMIT 1 (918-931).
findings.impact: A collection_item that has both a Pens detail (e.g. collection_detail_pen) and another family's detail (e.g. collection_detail_spinner) satisfies both families' checks, so collection_catalog_product can return either product and configuration-selection validation compares against a nondeterministic product.
findings.recommendation: Add a cross-family check that a collection_item has at most one detail family, or have collection_catalog_product reject items that map to more than one product.

findings.evidence: catalogProductType (index.ts:252-262) accepts only slider, slider-insert, slider-plate, spinner, and spinner-button and throws otherwise; the migration seeds catalog_terminology_concept rows for 'pen', 'pen-clip', 'pen-tip', 'pen-top-cap', 'pen-mechanism', 'pen-actuator', and 'refill' (migration.sql:497-504) and product_types rows for the same slugs.

findings.recommendation: Add the Pen and refill slugs to CatalogProductType (or stop narrowing in listTerminologyAliases/listProducts) so the service covers the concepts the migration creates.

findings.title: Unreachable maker guard and inner join hides maker-less aliases
findings.evidence: listTerminologyAliases inner-joins maker on catalogTerminologyAlias.makerId = maker.id (index.ts:3600-3603), so row.makerId is never null and the guard at 3609-3610 can never run. maker_id is now nullable (migration.sql:566), so a maker-less alias is dropped by the join before the guard would see it.
findings.impact: The guard suggests protection it cannot provide, and any global (maker-less) alias is silently absent from the list.
findings.recommendation: Either use a left join and handle a null makerId, or delete the guard and state that only maker-scoped aliases are returned.

findings.title: Unique constraints that no foreign key uses
findings.evidence: refill_offering_market_status_id_scope_unique (id, offering_id, market_id) at 462, refill_offering_identifier_id_scope_unique at 437, product_configuration_choice_id_slot_product_unique at 194, and product_configuration_choice_rule_id_target_product_unique at 217 are unique over a superset of the primary key, and no FOREIGN KEY in the migration references those column groups.
findings.impact: Each is an extra unique index maintained on every insert and update with no integrity benefit.
findings.recommendation: Drop the supersets and keep only the composite uniques the FKs actually reference (id, refill_product_id; id, slot_id; id, product_id; and rule id, product_id).

review.overview: PR #354 adds the normalized Pens catalog to the database package: 44 new tables plus a 1145-line migration that creates the tables, backfills the terminology-alias concept link, and installs many deferred constraint triggers enforcing cross-table invariants (product subtype, configuration carrier/rule rules, market containment, refill evidence and successor scope, append-only evidence). The alias table is reworked from a maker-scoped product-type alias into a concept-linked alias, collection items gain serial_number, and the services alias read/write path is updated to join the new concept table. Tests cover seeds, subtype validation, configuration rules, terminology collisions, market graphs and evidence requirements, but the owned-configuration-selection triggers are untested. The main risks are per-row full-table constraint triggers (quadratic on bulk import) and a NULL-semantics check that fails to enforce required explanation/remedy text.

findings.title: Per-row deferred constraint triggers scan whole tables, so bulk import is quadratic
findings.evidence: validate_refill_supporting_evidence() runs five full-table EXISTS scans (refill_offering, refill_offering_market_status, refill_offering_identifier, refill_compatibility_group_membership, refill_compatibility_assertion) and is attached with DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW to ten tables (lines 1050-1059). validate_refill_market_conflicts() (line 1067) builds a recursive closure over the entire catalog_market graph and self-joins all active statuses/identifiers, attached to three tables (lines 1132-1134). validate_catalog_terminology_aliases() (line 815) scans the alias/concept cross product.
findings.impact: A single INSERT ... SELECT that writes N rows queues N trigger executions at commit, each rescanning all rows, so cost is quadratic in table size. The same tables are the ones populated in bulk by source listings, choices and evidence imports, so a catalog import that is linear today becomes a timeout at scale. Assumed load: automated catalog ingestion writing many rows per transaction, not one row at a time.
findings.recommendation: Scope each validation function to the changed product/offering/market (use NEW/OLD keys instead of scanning all rows), or move the invariant into a statement-level constraint so it runs once per statement.

findings.title: Required explanation and remedy checks pass when the text column is NULL
findings.evidence: refill_compatibility_assertion_explanation_required is `outcome not in ('incompatible','variable') or char_length(trim(explanation)) between 1 and 2000`, and remedy_required is `outcome <> 'conditional' or char_length(trim(remedy)) between 1 and 2000` (mirrored in migration.sql:313-314). With explanation NULL, `FALSE OR NULL` evaluates to NULL, and a PostgreSQL CHECK passes on NULL.
findings.impact: An approved outcome of 'incompatible' or 'variable' can be stored with explanation NULL, and 'conditional' with remedy NULL, exactly the cases the constraint is meant to reject. Downstream presentation of incompatible/conditional refill claims can then show no reason or fix.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit IS NOT NULL, e.g. `outcome not in ('incompatible','variable') or (explanation is not null and char_length(trim(explanation)) between 1 and 2000)`, and the same for remedy.

findings.title: Nose-profile carrier rule is not re-checked when a product's type changes
findings.evidence: validate_pen_nose_profile_carrier() rejects assignments whose product_type is not 'pen' or 'pen-tip', but its only trigger is `AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON pen_nose_profile_assignment` (line 812). No trigger runs when product.product_type_id is updated.
findings.impact: Assign a nose profile to a product typed 'pen', then UPDATE that product to a spinner/slider type; the invalid assignment survives with no error, breaking the stated invariant that nose profiles belong only to Pens and Pen tips.
findings.recommendation: Add a trigger on product UPDATE OF product_type_id that re-runs this validation, or fold the nose-profile type check into validate_pens_product_detail().

findings.title: Owned configuration-selection triggers have no test
findings.evidence: validate_collection_configuration_selections() (migration.sql:933) enforces that a selection's slot belongs to the owned item's catalog product, that an installed part matches the choice and owner, and that an installed part is used once. Grepping the diff shows collection_item_configuration_selection appears only in schema, migration and docs, never in any test; pens-catalog.integration.test.ts exercises subtype, configuration-carrier, terminology, market and evidence rules but not these.
findings.impact: The most complex ownership rule (cross-item catalog matching plus per-owner install uniqueness) ships untested; a regression here is silent because nothing fails when the trigger is dropped or weakened.
findings.recommendation: Add integration cases: valid configuration selection, wrong-product slot rejection, cross-owner installed-part rejection, and installing one part twice.

findings.title: Schema permits maker-less terminology aliases but both service paths assume a maker
findings.evidence: catalogTerminologyAlias.makerId is now nullable and the preferred-scope check only requires a maker when isPreferred is true. But createTerminologyAlias requires input.makerId and inserts it, and listTerminologyAliases inner-joins maker on alias.makerId (packages/services/src/db/catalog/index.ts:3588), then throws if a returned makerId is null.
findings.impact: A global (maker_id NULL) alias inserted directly by a seed or future migration is invisible to listTerminologyAliases because the inner join drops it, and cannot be created through the service. The read model silently omits rows the schema allows.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the nullable maker_id to keep the invariant, or make listing use a left join and return global aliases explicitly.

findings.title: Redundant unique index on product_configuration_choice
findings.evidence: product_configuration_choice defines unique(id, slot_id, product_id), unique(id, slot_id), and unique(id, product_id). Every column set includes the primary key id, so all three are trivially unique. Only (id, slot_id) and (id, product_id) are referenced by foreign keys (choice_slot and rule/requirement targets); the three-column unique is referenced by nothing in the migration.
findings.impact: One extra index that must be written and vacuumed for no constraint benefit grows with the table.
findings.recommendation: Remove product_configuration_choice_id_slot_product_unique; check the same redundant three-column pattern on product_configuration_choice_rule.

review.overview: PR #376 adds material drill-downs to the public Trends page. It introduces a new public_collection_item_material_trend table, an exact catalog material-count query, privacy-safe collection item and collector material counts, three new material charts with equivalent tables, and stable materialId/materialSpecificId URL filters. This review read the full changed files and their direct callers, not only the diff.

findings.title: Material-specific lookup joins on material_specific id alone
findings.evidence: getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends left joins material_specific on material_specific.id = public_collection_item_material_trend.material_specific_id only. The new composite foreign key at packages/database/src/schema/trends.ts:98 references material_specific(material_id, id), so the unique key on material_specific is that pair, not id alone. The catalog query repeats the same id-only join at packages/services/src/db/trends/index.ts:185.
findings.impact: If two general materials reuse the same material_specific id, the join matches rows from the wrong material. That yields duplicated result rows, incorrect materialSpecificName and materialSpecificSlug, and duplicate React keys in MaterialTrendVisualization.
findings.recommendation: Join on both columns: eq(publicCollectionItemMaterialTrend.materialId, materialSpecific.materialId) and eq(publicCollectionItemMaterialTrend.materialSpecificId, materialSpecific.id). Apply the same fix to the catalog query at index.ts:185.

findings.title: Material aggregation duplicates the collection aggregation SQL
findings.evidence: The material refresh query re-declares the item_products union over the eleven collection_detail tables and repeats the eligible_items and scoped_items scoping already present in refreshPublicCollectionItemTrends at lines 427-456. The catalog query also repeats product eligibility rules used by listPublicProductTypeTrends.
findings.impact: Three copies of the same eligibility rules must change together. A future change to which items or products count will silently miss one copy.
findings.recommendation: Extract the item_products union and eligibility scoping into one shared SQL fragment, or compute material rows in the same pass as the existing collection aggregation.

findings.title: Exact catalog material aggregation runs on every public page load
findings.evidence: getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends runs a catalog-wide grouping-sets aggregation over product, product_types, product_material, materials, and material_specific. The Trends route loader calls it together with four other server functions on every anonymous request, with no cache or precomputation.
findings.impact: Anonymous Trends traffic pays the full aggregation cost each request, and the cost grows with catalog size.
findings.recommendation: Cache the exact catalog material aggregation, or compute and store it during the existing generation refresh like the other public Trends values.

findings.title: Collection material read has no ORDER BY while a test asserts order
findings.evidence: getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends selects rows with no orderBy. The integration test at packages/services/src/db/trends/index.integration.test.ts:90-106 asserts itemValues order as Steel then Titanium using toEqual on a filtered array.
findings.impact: The assertion depends on unspecified database row order and can flake. API consumers also cannot rely on any stable order.

findings.title: Uncaught error crash on continuous worker connection failure
findings.evidence: processContinuously creates a BullMQ Worker via #createWorker but registers no error event listener on the worker instance, whereas bounded process attaches worker.on('error', ...) at line 318.
findings.impact: When Redis disconnects or a command fails during continuous processing, BullMQ emits an error event on the Worker. In Node.js, an unhandled error event on an EventEmitter throws an uncaught exception that crashes the process immediately.
findings.recommendation: Attach an error listener to worker inside processContinuously or #createWorker to route transport failures to lifecycle events or a provided error callback.

findings.title: Double-fetch race condition reports accepted enqueue as false
findings.evidence: enqueue() calls this.#queue.add(...) and then executes const stored = await this.#queue.getJob(input.id), verifying stored?.opts.telemetry?.metadata === enqueueToken to set accepted.
findings.impact: If a concurrent worker executes and prunes the completed job before getJob() runs, stored resolves to null. enqueue() returns accepted: false even though the job was successfully persisted and executed. Because the mutex lock is already held, no conflicting job could have been inserted.
findings.recommendation: Return accepted: true immediately after this.#queue.add() resolves, removing the redundant getJob() call and eliminating the race with worker completion.

findings.title: Unattached volume on staged Redis causes startup failure with empty directory parameter
findings.evidence: sharedQueue executes /bin/sh -c "rm -rf $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH/lost+found/ && exec docker-entrypoint.sh redis-server ... --dir $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH", while redisVolume remains attached to legacyScraperQueue.

findings.title: Sequential enqueue loop introduces N+1 Redis round trips per batch
findings.evidence: enqueueMany() runs for (const input of inputs) results.push(await this.enqueue(input)), executing 5 to 6 sequential Redis round trips per item (SET NX lock, getJob, remove, add, getJob, EVAL unlock).
findings.impact: Producer scrapes generating hundreds of items incur thousands of serial network round trips over Redis. This introduces heavy latency into scheduled scraper executions and increases the risk of cron run timeouts compared to pipelined bulk enqueues.
findings.recommendation: Enqueue non-conflicting jobs concurrently with Promise.all or bundle deduplication and job insertion into a single Redis pipeline or Lua script.

findings.title: BullMQ defined queue ignores closed state
findings.evidence: BullMqDefinedQueue.prototype.close() closes #queue and active workers, but does not track or check a closed flag. In contrast, createInMemoryQueueAdapter guards methods with assertOpen(closed).
findings.impact: Invoking enqueue, process, counts, or redriveFailed on a closed queue continues executing against a closed BullMQ queue instance, producing unhandled rejections or silent hangs instead of fast failure.
findings.recommendation: Maintain a private #closed boolean flag set during close(), and assert that the queue is open at the entry of enqueue, enqueueMany, process, processContinuously, counts, and redriveFailed.

findings.title: Short reconnect retry strategy aborts after 1.5 seconds during Redis restarts

findings.impact: When Redis restarts or reloads AOF and RDB state during planned restart tests or Railway host maintenance, recovery often exceeds 1.5 seconds. Once retryStrategy returns null, ioredis marks the connection permanently closed and fails all subsequent queue operations until the process restarts.
findings.recommendation: Increase reconnect attempt limits or implement an exponential backoff capped at a maximum interval for production resilience.

findings.title: Staged Redis queue lacks attached volume and crashes on startup
findings.evidence: sharedQueue specifies startCommand with '--dir $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH', but railway.ts defines only one volume ('redis-volume') attached to legacyScraperQueue.

Deploying pocket-trash-queue leaves $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH unset; the start command executes 'rm -rf /lost+found/' and invokes redis-server with an empty '--dir' argument, causing container crash loops. Any written persistence is lost across restarts.
findings.recommendation: Declare a dedicated volume for pocket-trash-queue in railway.ts or adjust its start command until the legacy queue volume can be safely reassigned.

findings.title: Sequential per-item locking in enqueueMany causes major producer latency
findings.evidence: enqueueMany iterates over inputs sequentially with 'for (const input of inputs) results.push(await this.enqueue(input))', where each enqueue acquires a separate Redis lock and executes 6-7 round trips.
findings.impact: Grimsmo and Autmog producers enqueuing hundreds or thousands of products execute thousands of serial Redis round trips instead of pipelining via addBulk. Cross-service network latency adds tens of seconds, risking 5-minute scraper cron timeouts.
findings.recommendation: Pipeline batch insertions or execute non-conflicting job enqueues concurrently using BullMQ's native addBulk mechanism.

findings.title: Redundant getJob network call on every enqueue
findings.evidence: enqueue executes 'await this.#queue.add(...)' and immediately follows with 'const stored = await this.#queue.getJob(input.id)' to inspect telemetry metadata.
findings.impact: BullMQ queue.add already returns the created Job instance. Calling getJob introduces an extra network round trip for every enqueued job, doubling latency and risking false negatives if an active worker completes and removes the job before getJob resolves.
findings.recommendation: Inspect the Job object returned directly by this.#queue.add instead of issuing an extra getJob query.

findings.title: Unbounded busy-wait loop during enqueue lock contention
findings.evidence: The do-while loop in enqueue polls this.#connection.set with NX and 30-second PX every 10 milliseconds without a timeout or maximum attempt count.
findings.impact: If an enqueue operation crashes or terminates while holding the lock key, competing calls will spin 3,000 times over 30 seconds before proceeding, hanging producers or request handlers.
findings.recommendation: Cap the maximum lock acquisition attempts or timeout duration, and reduce the 30-second lease to match fast Redis operations.

findings.title: BullMQ adapter ignores closed state and violates queue contract
findings.evidence: BullMqDefinedQueue does not track closure or assert open state on enqueue, counts, process, or redriveFailed, unlike the in-memory adapter assertOpen check.
findings.impact: Calling operations on a closed BullMQ queue leaks internal Redis connection errors from disconnecting clients instead of throwing the standardized contract error 'Queue is closed.'.
findings.recommendation: Add an internal closed flag and assertOpen guard to BullMqDefinedQueue methods to match createInMemoryQueueAdapter.

findings.title: Adapter Redis connection retry strategy permanently terminates after 3 attempts
findings.evidence: retryStrategy specifies 'return times <= 3 ? Math.min(times * 250, 1_000) : null;'.
findings.impact: If Redis restarts or takes more than ~1.75 seconds during host failover or restart testing, ioredis stops reconnecting and permanently closes the client. The adapter cannot recover without a complete service restart.
findings.recommendation: Allow reconnect attempts to continue with capped backoff rather than returning null after 3 attempts.

findings.title: Deterministic mock clock desynchronization stalls in-memory continuous worker retries
findings.evidence: processContinuously sets a real setTimeout for Math.max(0, retryAt - now()), and the callback checks 'if (now() >= retryAt) wake()' against the custom now function.
findings.impact: When tests supply a deterministic clock that is not manually advanced before the real setTimeout fires, the condition evaluates to false, retryTimer becomes undefined, and delayed jobs stall indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Expose an explicit clock promotion or flush method for test adapters rather than coupling mock timestamps with real timers.

review.overview: PR #354 adds the normalized Pens catalog schema, modeling pens, modular components, refill offerings, interchangeability claims, product configuration slots, markets, and provenance evidence. While the normalized schema and subtype hierarchy are well structured, catalog service helpers will crash at runtime due to obsolete product-type restrictions, deferred constraint triggers introduce race-condition and full-table scan vulnerabilities under concurrent load, and several redundant indexes and procedural triggers should be simplified into declarative PostgreSQL constraints.

findings.title: Catalog alias service crashes on non-legacy product types and terminology concepts
findings.evidence: In packages/services/src/db/catalog/index.ts at line 3613, listTerminologyAliases maps every alias row through catalogProductType(row.canonicalKey). catalogProductType at lines 252-263 only supports five legacy spinner/slider slugs ('slider', 'slider-insert', 'slider-plate', 'spinner', 'spinner-button') and throws an exception for all other strings. The migration seeded seven new product types ('pen', 'pen-clip', 'pen-tip', 'pen-top-cap', 'pen-mechanism', 'pen-actuator', 'refill') and removed the constraint restricting aliases to product-type. createTerminologyAlias at line 2425 similarly rejects any new product type.
findings.impact: Calling listTerminologyAliases or createTerminologyAlias for pens, pen parts, refills, or any non-product-type concept namespace (such as pen-part-role or refill-compatibility-group) throws an unhandled exception and crashes catalog terminology operations.
findings.recommendation: Expand CatalogProductType and catalogProductType to include the new pen product types. In listTerminologyAliases, add a WHERE filter for canonicalNamespace = 'product-type' or generalize the return type to support arbitrary registered terminology concepts.

findings.title: Installed pen part uniqueness relies on a non-atomic trigger scan instead of a unique index
findings.evidence: In packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts at line 746, installedPartCollectionItemId is defined with a non-unique index. In migration.sql lines 956-963, uniqueness is enforced via a PL/pgSQL trigger query: SELECT installed_part_collection_item_id FROM collection_item_configuration_selection WHERE installed_part_collection_item_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY installed_part_collection_item_id HAVING count(*) > 1.
findings.impact: Under PostgreSQL's default Read Committed transaction isolation, concurrent transactions installing the same part into different parent pens cannot see each other's uncommitted rows during the trigger query. Both transactions commit successfully, violating the business rule and creating duplicate installations. In addition, every row write forces an expensive full-table aggregation scan.
findings.recommendation: Replace the non-unique index and procedural trigger check with a partial unique index: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX collection_item_configuration_selection_installed_part_unique ON collection_item_configuration_selection (installed_part_collection_item_id) WHERE installed_part_collection_item_id IS NOT NULL;.

findings.title: Row-level deferred constraint triggers execute expensive global table scans across unrelated tables
findings.evidence: In packages/database/drizzle/20261010021729_pens_catalog_schema/migration.sql at lines 1012-1058, validate_refill_supporting_evidence executes five full-table EXISTS subqueries across five distinct entities whenever any row changes in ten separate tables. Similarly, lines 1066-1133 run recursive CTEs over the entire market containment graph for each row inserted, updated, or deleted in refill_offering_market_status and refill_offering_identifier.
findings.impact: Batch imports, catalog updates, and automated migrations suffer quadratic O(N^2) query amplification, severe lock contention, and high transaction latency because each row modification re-scans entire tables and re-evaluates unrelated domains.
findings.recommendation: Scope row triggers to inspect NEW and OLD rows instead of scanning entire tables. Change whole-table validation triggers from FOR EACH ROW to FOR EACH STATEMENT, and remove AFTER DELETE triggers on tables where deletions cannot introduce integrity violations.

findings.title: Successor scope uses procedural trigger checks instead of declarative composite foreign keys
findings.evidence: In packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts at lines 980 and 1058, composite unique constraints exist on refill_offering_market_status(id, offering_id, market_id) and refill_offering_identifier(id, maker_id, kind, market_id). However, successorId at lines 971 and 1051 references only id, leaving scope preservation to a procedural trigger function validate_refill_successors (migration.sql lines 991-1008).
findings.impact: Adds procedural trigger overhead and redundant table scans on every status and identifier update, while maintaining composite unique indexes that serve no foreign key reference.
findings.recommendation: Change successorId foreign keys to composite foreign keys referencing (successor_id, offering_id, market_id) and (successor_id, maker_id, kind, market_id). Delete validate_refill_successors and its associated triggers.

blockingFindingsForAdjudication.title: Catalog alias service crashes on non-legacy product types and terminology concepts
blockingFindingsForAdjudication.evidence: In packages/services/src/db/catalog/index.ts at line 3613, listTerminologyAliases maps every alias row through catalogProductType(row.canonicalKey). catalogProductType at lines 252-263 only supports five legacy spinner/slider slugs ('slider', 'slider-insert', 'slider-plate', 'spinner', 'spinner-button') and throws an exception for all other strings. The migration seeded seven new product types ('pen', 'pen-clip', 'pen-tip', 'pen-top-cap', 'pen-mechanism', 'pen-actuator', 'refill') and removed the constraint restricting aliases to product-type. createTerminologyAlias at line 2425 similarly rejects any new product type.
blockingFindingsForAdjudication.impact: Calling listTerminologyAliases or createTerminologyAlias for pens, pen parts, refills, or any non-product-type concept namespace (such as pen-part-role or refill-compatibility-group) throws an unhandled exception and crashes catalog terminology operations.
blockingFindingsForAdjudication.recommendation: Expand CatalogProductType and catalogProductType to include the new pen product types. In listTerminologyAliases, add a WHERE filter for canonicalNamespace = 'product-type' or generalize the return type to support arbitrary registered terminology concepts.

blockingFindingsForAdjudication.title: Installed pen part uniqueness relies on a non-atomic trigger scan instead of a unique index
blockingFindingsForAdjudication.evidence: In packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts at line 746, installedPartCollectionItemId is defined with a non-unique index. In migration.sql lines 956-963, uniqueness is enforced via a PL/pgSQL trigger query: SELECT installed_part_collection_item_id FROM collection_item_configuration_selection WHERE installed_part_collection_item_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY installed_part_collection_item_id HAVING count(*) > 1.
blockingFindingsForAdjudication.impact: Under PostgreSQL's default Read Committed transaction isolation, concurrent transactions installing the same part into different parent pens cannot see each other's uncommitted rows during the trigger query. Both transactions commit successfully, violating the business rule and creating duplicate installations. In addition, every row write forces an expensive full-table aggregation scan.
blockingFindingsForAdjudication.recommendation: Replace the non-unique index and procedural trigger check with a partial unique index: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX collection_item_configuration_selection_installed_part_unique ON collection_item_configuration_selection (installed_part_collection_item_id) WHERE installed_part_collection_item_id IS NOT NULL;.

review.overview: PR #354 introduces a normalized relational schema for Pens, modular pen components, refill offerings, market availability, evidence provenance, and product configuration choices. It adds 23 tables, backfills terminology concepts from product types, and enforces relational integrity via deferred PL/pgSQL constraint triggers. While the core database migrations and schemas are solid, the catalog service terminology queries crash when encountering new pen product types or concepts, and the market conflict trigger incurs quadratic graph-walking overhead during batch operations.

findings.title: Terminology alias queries and mutations crash on new pen product types
findings.evidence: listTerminologyAliases passes row.canonicalKey into catalogProductType() without filtering canonicalNamespace = 'product-type'. catalogProductType only accepts slider and spinner slugs, throwing an uncaught error on newly seeded product types (pen, pen-clip, refill) or non-product-type concepts. Additionally, createTerminologyAlias at line 2425 validates input.canonicalKey against catalogProductType, rejecting attempts to alias any new pen product type.
findings.impact: Calling listTerminologyAliases crashes with an unhandled exception whenever an alias exists for a pen product type or a non-product-type concept. Administrators cannot register terminology aliases for pens or pen parts.
findings.recommendation: Extend CatalogProductType and catalogProductType() to support all new pen and refill slugs ('pen', 'pen-clip', 'pen-tip', 'pen-top-cap', 'pen-mechanism', 'pen-actuator', 'refill'). In listTerminologyAliases, add .where(eq(schema.catalogTerminologyAlias.canonicalNamespace, 'product-type')) to restrict the query to product-type concepts.

findings.title: Refill market conflict constraint triggers perform unindexed full-table graph traversal
findings.evidence: validate_refill_market_conflicts computes recursive reachability across the entire catalog_market hierarchy and executes an unconstrained cross-join on all active offering statuses and identifiers. Because the constraint triggers on refill_offering_market_status and refill_offering_identifier run FOR EACH ROW and include DELETE events, bulk transactions recompute the full transitive graph for every row without filtering on NEW or OLD offering IDs.
findings.impact: Batch inserts or updates of market statuses and identifiers degrade to O(N * M^2) execution time. Transactions face high latency and lock contention as catalog data grows.
findings.recommendation: Filter the conflict validation queries by COALESCE(NEW.offering_id, OLD.offering_id) and COALESCE(NEW.maker_id, OLD.maker_id). Remove the unnecessary OR DELETE trigger events on status and identifier tables since deleting records cannot introduce market conflicts.

findings.title: Collection item ownership changes bypass configuration selection owner consistency
findings.evidence: validate_collection_configuration_selections ensures parent.owner_id matches installed.owner_id for installed pen parts. However, trigger collection_configuration_selection_valid is attached only to collection_item_configuration_selection. Updating collection_item.owner_id directly does not invoke validation.
findings.impact: Transferring or selling an installed pen component updates collection_item.owner_id without trigger validation, leaving the parent pen with an installed part owned by another user.
findings.recommendation: Add a deferred constraint trigger on collection_item AFTER UPDATE OF owner_id that invokes validate_collection_configuration_selections().

findings.title: Collection item configuration selection logic lacks integration test coverage
findings.evidence: pens-catalog.integration.test.ts tests catalog configuration slots and choices, but contains zero assertions targeting collection_item_configuration_selection or validate_collection_configuration_selections.
findings.impact: Regressions in slot compatibility, ownership mismatch validation, or multiple-installation prevention will not be detected by CI.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests verifying that configuration selections succeed for matching owned parts, fail when slot products or owners mismatch, and reject installing an owned part into multiple pens.

findings.title: Product entity relations omit inverse nose profile assignment
findings.evidence: penNoseProfileAssignment defines a one-to-one relation pointing to product, and catalogTerminologyConcept defines noseProfiles. However, the product relation definition in relations.ts does not declare an inverse noseProfile relation.
findings.impact: Callers cannot traverse or query a product's assigned nose profile using Drizzle relational queries (such as db.query.product.findMany({ with: { noseProfile: true } })).
findings.recommendation: Add noseProfile: r.one.penNoseProfileAssignment() to the product relation object in packages/database/src/schema/relations.ts.

review.overview: This PR adds a private `@package/queue` package. It exposes a transport-independent queue contract, a BullMQ/Redis adapter and an in-memory adapter. The scraper's queue module, producers and processor move onto it, and the scraper now builds its own BullMQ adapter from `REDIS_URL`. It also stages a second Railway Redis resource, `pocket-trash-queue`, with RDB and AOF persistence, and keeps the legacy `scraper-queue`. Railpack, `.railwayignore`, CI and docs changes come with it. The scraper migration looks behavior-preserving: queue names, retry and retention policy, drain semantics and dead-letter redrive carry over. The main risks are in the new package and the infrastructure staging. The Redis reconnect policy gives up after about 1.5 seconds, which will break the planned long-lived workers. Payload schemas are not type-linked to the job types they validate. The new Redis resource shows no volume attachment in the IaC. Several docs describe the shared queue as live although preview and production still point at `scraper-queue`. No code or infrastructure was executed. Findings come from reading the diff and the added files.

findings.title: Redis reconnect gives up after three attempts, which breaks long-lived workers
findings.evidence: `retryStrategy` returns `null` once `times > 3`, so ioredis stops reconnecting after roughly 250+500+750 ms. The `connection.on("error")` handler at line 49 is empty. `#createWorker` registers no `error` listener on the worker, and `processContinuously` never surfaces connection errors.
findings.impact: The package defines a `continuous` mode for the Discord bot, and the docs say the bot will share this Redis. A Railway Redis restart or redeploy takes longer than about 1.5 seconds. After that the connection is permanently closed, the continuous worker stops receiving jobs, and nothing reports it. The bounded scraper cron is unaffected because the process exits after each run.
findings.recommendation: Use a retry strategy that backs off up to a cap and never returns null for the shared connection. Alternatively, pass the policy in per adapter and default it to unlimited for continuous queues. Report connection and worker errors through `onEvent`, with a new `error` event type, instead of swallowing them. Add a contract or integration test that restarts Redis while a continuous worker is open.

findings.title: Queue payload schemas are not type-linked to the job types they validate
findings.evidence: `scraperItemJobSchema` and `scraperImageJobSchema` use `z.custom<ScraperItemJob>(value => schema.safeParse(value).success)`. That asserts the TypeScript type without checking that the hand-written zod shapes match it. The shapes copy every field of the normalized Autmog and Grimsmo items, for example `sourceImageId: z.string().nullable()` and `variants: z.array(z.json())`. The only test for this is one malformed-payload case in `queues.test.ts`.
findings.impact: If a normalizer later adds, renames or makes a field optional, the code still compiles. A producer then either throws at enqueue and aborts the run, or persists a payload that fails validation at delivery. A job rejected at delivery is retried 5 times with exponential backoff (30 s base) and then held in the failed set for 7 days. The decision record promises that retained jobs stay compatible, but no test enqueues real normalizer output or a payload shaped like the old format.
findings.recommendation: Make the link checkable at compile time. For example, build the schemas as `z.ZodType<ScraperItemJob>` with `satisfies`, or add a type-level equality assertion between `z.infer` of the payload schema and `ScraperItemJob`. Add a test that runs real Autmog and Grimsmo normalizer fixtures through `enqueue`. Add another test that feeds a payload captured from the previous release.

findings.title: New shared Redis resource shows no persistent volume, but its start command and the docs assume one
findings.evidence: `sharedQueue` runs `rm -rf $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH/lost+found/ && ... --dir $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH` with `--appendonly yes`. The only volume declared is `redisVolume`, described as the existing volume that is retained without changing its mount, and it belongs to the legacy `scraper-queue`. The docs say `pocket-trash-queue` uses `redis-volume` and shares its 5 GB. The same docs also say staging must not detach `scraper-queue` or `redis-volume`. The reviewed plan only reports `1 to add`.
findings.impact: A Railway volume mounts on one service. If the new database does not get its own volume, `$RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH` is empty. Then `--dir` has no argument and Redis fails to start, or RDB/AOF write to ephemeral disk. In that case the documented persistence guarantee, the 1 GiB reservation and the restart test in stage 2 of the migration plan all fail. This would surface during the later provisioning stage, not in this PR's tests.
findings.recommendation: Declare the volume for `pocket-trash-queue` explicitly in the IaC, or document that the Railway `redis()` template creates its own, and fix the docs. Do not describe the legacy volume as shared. Extend `railway-config.test.mjs` to assert that the new queue has a volume. Check the plan output for the added volume.

findings.title: Enqueue is serial with about six Redis round trips per job and an unbounded lock wait
findings.evidence: Each `enqueue` runs `SET NX`, `getJob`, `getState` when a job exists, `queue.add`, a second `getJob`, and an `EVAL`. `enqueueMany` awaits these one at a time. The `do ... while (acquired !== "OK")` loop has no overall deadline. The 30 s lock lease is never renewed. The old path was `getJob` per id followed by one `addBulk`.
findings.impact: I assumed batches of hundreds of jobs. Grimsmo produces one job per variation plus a batch job, and the processor enqueues image jobs per item. A batch of 500 now costs about 3,000 sequential round trips. That is seconds on the private network, but could be much longer if `REDIS_URL` goes through the public TCP proxy. A stuck lock holder blocks other enqueuers for up to 30 s with no error. If an enqueue exceeds the lease, two writers can overlap.
findings.recommendation: Add a maximum wait that throws, and run independent ids with bounded concurrency (for example 16). Keep per-id ordering. Alternatively, move the check-and-add into one Lua script, which removes the lock and most round trips. Record the assumed batch size in a comment.

findings.title: Enqueue acceptance depends on BullMQ's telemetry field being persisted
findings.evidence: A random token is written to `telemetry.metadata` with `omitContext: true`. The job is read back, and `accepted` is true only if `stored.opts.telemetry?.metadata` equals the token. This uses a tracing option as a write-ownership marker. It relies on BullMQ persisting and returning that value without a tracer configured, and on `omitContext` keeping the user value.
findings.impact: If a BullMQ upgrade changes how `telemetry` options are stored or merged, `accepted` flips to false for every new job. Producers then log nothing wrong and nothing gets enqueued as reported. Only the Redis integration test would notice, and it needs a local `redis-server`.
findings.recommendation: Drop the lock and token pair for a short Lua script that checks for the job and then adds it. It returns an explicit accepted or already-exists value. If the token approach stays, add a comment naming the BullMQ version it depends on and keep the integration test required in CI.

findings.title: New queue keeps a public TCP proxy although consumers use the private URL
findings.evidence: `sharedQueue.networking` sets `tcpProxies: { "6379": {} }`, copied from the legacy resource. The docs tell both apps to use `${{pocket-trash-queue.REDIS_URL}}`, which is the private-network URL. The same docs say the queue will hold Discord ticket data and account-linked notification jobs.
findings.impact: Redis would be reachable from the internet, protected only by its password. That adds exposure for a store the erasure matrix classifies as holding restricted personal data, and the proxy has no consumer.
findings.recommendation: Remove the TCP proxy from `pocket-trash-queue`, or document who needs public access and why. Keep it only on the legacy resource, which still needs it for the existing reference.

findings.title: Install command is defined in three places, and the railpack.json form may skip default install setup
findings.evidence: The same command string `./scripts/pnpm-install.sh --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` now lives in `railpack.json` (`steps.install.commands`), in the IaC `RAILPACK_INSTALL_CMD` env at `.railway/railway.ts:104`, and in two new `railway variable set` calls in `deploy.yml`. The only test for the new file asserts that its JSON equals this string.
findings.impact: Three copies can drift apart. The env override only changes the install command. I did not confirm Railpack's behavior for a custom `commands` array. If it replaces the whole default install step, the first native PR build may lack the manifest copy and cache setup, and fail. The test cannot catch that.
findings.recommendation: Check a native PR build on a branch against the Railpack docs, and include the spread of default commands if required. After that, keep a single source: remove either the `railpack.json` step or the workflow `variable set` calls, and state the reason in `docs/railway.md`.

findings.title: Docs and diagram describe the staged queue as live
findings.evidence: The erasure matrix replaces the `scraper-queue` row with `pocket-trash-queue`, which includes Discord ticket data. The docs say the preview workflow keeps using `scraper-queue` until cutover. `docs/infrastructure-diagram.yaml` (line 74) draws production and preview scrapers writing to `pocket-trash-queue` and labels `dev_queue` as Railway. The Discord bot is not in this PR. `docs/railway.md` also says the migration is only staged.
findings.impact: Until cutover, the live scraper data sits in `scraper-queue`, which no longer appears in the erasure or region tables. An erasure operator following the matrix would not inspect the actual live store or its backups. The diagram shows an unfinished state as current.
findings.recommendation: Keep the `scraper-queue` rows in the erasure matrix and region table until cleanup is approved. Mark `pocket-trash-queue` rows and diagram edges as staged, or add them at cutover. Label the dev queue as local Redis instead of Railway.

findings.title: Test suite now requires a local redis-server binary with no skip path
findings.evidence: CI adds an unpinned `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install --yes redis-server`. `bullmq.integration.test.ts` spawns `redis-server` in `beforeAll` and fails if the binary is missing. `waitForRedis` waits for the text `Ready to accept connections` and has no timeout beyond the test runner's. `afterAll` sends SIGTERM and does not wait for exit.
findings.impact: Any developer or other workflow that runs `pnpm test` without Redis installed gets a failing package, not a skip. A different Redis version on the CI image can change the startup log line and hang the suite. A leftover process can hold the port.
findings.recommendation: Skip the integration suite when `redis-server` is not found, with a clear message. Add a startup timeout that rejects with the captured stderr. Await process exit in `afterAll`. Optionally use a pinned service container in CI instead of apt.

review.overview: The PR moves scraper queues from direct BullMQ use to a new `@package/queue` package. The package has a BullMQ adapter, an in-memory test adapter and a shared contract test suite. It also adds a second Railway Redis, `pocket-trash-queue`, next to the legacy `scraper-queue`. The scraper still uses the legacy queue, so the new one is staged only. I found no critical or high issues. The main risks are: the hand-written Zod payload schemas are never checked against real producer output, the IaC does not say which volume the new Redis uses, and the BullMQ adapter's reconnect policy is unsafe for the planned long-running bot. Smaller issues are slower sequential enqueues, lost drain and redrive logging, and a Redis binary requirement for tests. I did not run tests or inspect installed BullMQ code.

findings.title: Payload schemas are hand-copied and never tested against real producer output
findings.evidence: `scraperItemJobSchema` is `z.custom<ScraperItemJob>(value => scraperItemPayloadSchema.safeParse(value).success)`, so the compiler never compares it with `NormalizedAutmogPen` or the Grimsmo types. The failure message is a fixed string with no Zod path. The producer tests (`autmog/producer.test.ts`, `grimsmo/producer.test.ts`) replace `enqueueMany` with `vi.fn()`. The only schema test (`queues.test.ts`) sends `{ sourceHandle: 1 }` and expects rejection. I compared the top-level fields of the pen, knife and Saga types with the schemas and they match. I could not see `AutmogPenNormalizedData` or `GrimsmoVariationImageRecord`. `variants` is typed `unknown[]` but validated with `z.array(z.json())`, which rejects `undefined` values.
findings.impact: Every enqueue and every delivery goes through these schemas. If a normalizer emits `undefined` where the schema expects `null`, or a nested field drifts, every producer run throws in production. No unit test would have caught it. Jobs already in Redis would also fail five times each and land in the failed set.
findings.recommendation: Add one test that runs real normalizer output (Autmog pen, Grimsmo pen, knife, Saga snapshot) through `createScraperQueues(..., createInMemoryQueueAdapter()).items.enqueue`. Add a compile-time check that the schema output matches `ScraperItemJob`, for example `satisfies z.ZodType<ScraperItemJob>` instead of `z.custom`. Include the Zod issue path in the thrown error.

findings.title: New Redis service has no declared volume, and the docs say it shares the legacy volume
findings.evidence: `sharedQueue` starts Redis with `--dir $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH` and AOF enabled. The only volume in the IaC is `redis-volume`, and nothing in this file binds it to either Redis. `docs/railway.md` says `pocket-trash-queue` uses the Railway Redis template 'with `redis-volume`' and that both apps share 'the 5 GB `redis-volume`'. Migration step 1 says to provision the new service 'without deleting or detaching `scraper-queue` or `redis-volume`'. The railway-config test only checks that the start command contains the persistence flags.
findings.impact: A Railway volume attaches to one service, so the new Redis cannot mount the volume the legacy Redis still holds. If it has no volume, the variable is empty and Redis fails to start on the `--dir` argument. If Railway adds its own volume, its size and alerts are not in the IaC, and the 5 GB and 1 GiB capacity planning in the docs is wrong. The persistence promised by RDB and AOF may not exist.
findings.recommendation: Declare the volume that `pocket-trash-queue` uses, with its size and alerts, in `.railway/railway.ts`. Rewrite the docs to say whether the new Redis gets its own volume or takes over `redis-volume` after cutover. Add a test that the IaC binds a volume to the new Redis.

findings.title: Reconnect policy permanently kills the shared Redis connection after about 1.5 seconds
findings.evidence: `retryStrategy` returns `null` after 3 attempts (250, 500, 750 ms). The connection `error` handler is empty, and `#createWorker` registers no `error` listener for continuous workers. `processContinuously` is part of the public contract, and the ADR says the bot will share this package.
findings.impact: A Redis restart or Railway redeploy of the shared instance that lasts longer than about 1.5 seconds leaves the ioredis connection permanently ended. A long-running bot worker would stop consuming jobs while the process stays up, with no event telling the app. The scraper cron recovers on its next run, so it is mostly unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Make the retry policy depend on queue mode. Use unbounded capped backoff for continuous workers, and keep the short limit for bounded drains. Surface worker and connection errors to the caller, for example through `onEvent` or a `QueueWorker` error hook. Add a contract test that restarts Redis while a continuous worker is open.

findings.title: Enqueue takes five or six Redis round trips per job and re-reads the full payload
findings.evidence: `enqueue` does SET NX for the lock, `getJob`, `getState`, `add`, a second `getJob` to compare the telemetry token, then an `eval` to release the lock. `enqueueMany` (line 249) runs this sequentially per job. The old code did one `getJob` and `getState` per id, then a single `addBulk`. `getJob` returns the whole payload, and batch jobs carry whole feeds. `deploy.yml` line 664 points previews at `REDIS_PUBLIC_URL`, and the removed docs line did the same for production.
findings.impact: Over the public Redis proxy, a run enqueuing thousands of jobs takes roughly three times longer than before, and payload bytes are read back several times. The scraper runs on a 5-minute cron, so the cost is wasted time rather than a failure.
findings.recommendation: Keep correctness but cut the round trips. Pipeline the lock and existence check, or use one Lua script that checks state and adds the job. Stop reading the payload back, for example by checking the add result or reading `opts` only. Switch to the private `REDIS_URL` at cutover.

findings.title: Drain and redrive logging was removed, and lifecycle events are not wired up
findings.evidence: `createScraperQueues` calls `createBullMqQueueAdapter({ redisUrl })` without `onEvent`, so the started, completed and failed events have no consumer. The deleted `drainQueue` logged `scraper.queue.drainCompleted` and `drainFailed`. The deleted `processDeadLetters` logged each failed requeue with `failedReason`, `attemptsMade` and the queue name. The new `redriveFailed` (`bullmq.ts` line 370) catches the error and only increments `requeueFailed`.
findings.impact: When a redrive fails, the logs show a count and nothing about which job or why. A worker error now ends the drain without the queue-level log line. This hurts debugging an unattended cron.
findings.recommendation: Pass an `onEvent` that logs through the scraper logger. Have `redriveFailed` report per-job failures, such as id and reason, or emit them as events. Remove any logger messages that are now unused.

findings.title: Integration test needs a `redis-server` binary and has no skip path
findings.evidence: `beforeAll` runs `spawn("redis-server", ...)`. The PR installs Redis with `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install --yes redis-server` in one `ci.yml` job only. The package's `test`, `test:ci` and `test:watch` scripts all run vitest over this file.
findings.impact: Any developer without Redis installed gets a failing `pnpm test`. Any other CI job that runs this package's tests fails the same way. The apt update adds time to every CI run.
findings.recommendation: Skip the suite with a clear message when `redis-server` is missing. Alternatively, run it under a separate script and document the requirement. Keep the in-memory contract tests in the default run.

findings.title: Same install command lives in four places
findings.evidence: `./scripts/pnpm-install.sh --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` is set in `railpack.json`, as `RAILPACK_INSTALL_CMD` in `.railway/railway.ts` line 104, and in two new `deploy.yml` blocks (preview and production). `scripts/railway-config.test.mjs` and `scripts/change-classification.test.mjs` each assert one of these copies. The docs say `railpack.json` exists because native PR builds run before Actions sets variables.
findings.impact: The copies can drift apart, and each needs its own test. I could not confirm whether Railpack treats `steps.install.commands` as a full replacement that drops the default install setup.
findings.recommendation: Keep `railpack.json` as the only source, since it covers the first native build. Delete the IaC env entry and the two `deploy.yml` blocks, with their test assertions. If the env var is needed, document why and keep a single test.
